transcript: one of the most anticipated new musicals of the season has music and lyrics by Sia and tells the story of a black gay teenager named Ulysses who finds solace in a queer community Shelter Saturday Church is based on the 2017 film of the same name and boasts an incredible team of artists including Pulitzer winner James Ijames, who wrote Fat Ham Whitney White one of the most in-demand directors in the industry right now and a ridiculously talented cast that includes Tony winners Joaquina Kalukanga, J Harrison Ghee and led by Bryson Battle from The Voice the book in some ways I found to be a little bit predictable a little bit saccharine dare I say even a little bit trite at times but I think they get away with it for several reasons first of all even where it's kinda like “maybe we've seen stories like this before” “maybe we kinda know where it's going” “what the messaging is gonna be” in the end it does, unfortunately feel as relevant and urgent as ever due to the times we're living in and there are ways in which they approach it from different perspectives like one of the recurring themes I was struck most by in the story is how all of the adults in Ulysses life kind of project their past experiences and their relationship to queerness, or the queer community on to him I also just think everyone here is wearing their hearts on their sleeves in a palpable way where even in a scene or a plot beat that didn't totally click for me from a writing standpoint I feel like the cast, along with the direction from Whitney White, just completely sells it because you can tell that they believe it and are feeling it with their entire chest and for that matter I also thought the musicalization was pretty strong now I believe this is a mix of existing Sia songs as well as new ones that she wrote for the musical I actually don't know what the percentage was and maybe that itself is kind of a compliment to the show and how they constructed the score for the story so her music along with additional music by Honey Dijon and the choreography and the fantastic lighting design everything just kind of comes together to create this exhilarating, infectious energy that leans into just the right blend of emotion, drama, and joy
